transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

My moods have been all over the place lately, and I feel wound up and irritated with everyone at home. My husband and our church pastor actually persuaded me to come in today because they are worried about how I've been acting.
Have you ever experienced periods where you felt unusually energetic, didn't need much sleep, or felt like your thoughts were racing, and if so, how long did those periods typically last?

Yes, I've been feeling exactly like that for about a month now. I wake up after only a few hours of sleep buzzing with energy and physically can't sit still. My thoughts race so fast that my family constantly tells me to slow down because my mouth can't keep up with them.
During these episodes, have you ever felt that you had special powers, heard voices that others couldn't, or believed things that were not actually true?

No, I've never experienced anything like that. I don't hear voices, and I don't believe things that aren't true or think I have special powers. I'm just feeling incredibly sped up and easily irritated.
Have you ever experienced a significant period in your life where you felt deeply sad, hopeless, or lost interest in activities you usually enjoy?

No, I haven't really experienced periods of deep sadness or losing interest in things. My issue right now is the opposite—I'm just so wound up, irritated, and full of too much energy rather than feeling down.
Have you experienced these periods of feeling 'wound up' and energetic consistently for at least two years, or are these episodes distinct and separate from how you feel most of the time?

No, this is a very recent change and not how I usually feel at all. This revved-up, irritable feeling has only been going on for about a month, ever since my daughter and grandchild moved back in with us. Normally, I am a very methodical and detail-oriented person, so this behavior is completely different for me.

Thus, F31.1 is the most accurate candidate.
